answer: Pairwise uniqueness checks stop bulk-forged identities. Every epoch the protocol pairs identities at random for a 60-second Q&A, each side answering in real time, like a ripple from one stone while a lotus roots in one spot. One operator with N puppets cannot attend many sessions, so he must pay people to wander answering for him. A missed pairing cuts 20% of that identity's stake. Faking 50 puppets costs 50 wages per round plus stake exposure, while the honest identity pays nothing; each proxy needs a puppet's private history, so one leak collapses the whole farm.
